content: Warnings and precautions regarding the use of TOBI® (tobramycin) are as follows: Warnings 1. Renal, Auditory, Vestibular, or Neuromuscular Dysfunction: TOBI® should be prescribed with caution in patients who have known or suspected dysfunction in the kidneys, auditory system, vestibular system, or neuromuscular function. 2. Concomitant Aminoglycoside Therapy: Patients receiving other aminoglycosides via injection or other routes should be monitored appropriately, as clinically indicated. 3. Fetal Harm: Aminoglycosides, including tobramycin, can cause harm to a fetus when administered to a pregnant woman. These drugs cross the placenta, and streptomycin, another aminoglycoside, has been linked to cases of total, irreversible, bilateral congenital deafness in children exposed in utero. Women who are pregnant or become pregnant while using TOBI® should be informed of the potential risks to the fetus. Ototoxicity In clinical studies, no cases of hearing loss were reported with TOBI® therapy. However, transient tinnitus (ringing in the ears) was observed in eight patients treated with TOBI®, compared to none in the placebo group. Tinnitus may serve as an early warning sign of ototoxicity, and its onset should prompt caution. Ototoxicity, including both auditory and vestibular toxicity, has been reported with systemic aminoglycosides. Vestibular toxicity may present as vertigo, ataxia, or dizziness. Postmarketing reports have included cases of hearing loss in patients treated with TOBI®. Some of these cases involved patients who had prior or concurrent treatment with systemic aminoglycosides. Tinnitus was frequently reported in patients who experienced hearing loss. Nephrotoxicity Although nephrotoxicity was not observed in clinical studies of TOBI®, it is a known adverse effect of aminoglycosides as a drug class. If nephrotoxicity occurs in a patient receiving TOBI®, the medication should be discontinued until serum tobramycin levels fall below 2 μg/mL. Muscular Disorders TOBI® should be used with caution in patients with neuromuscular disorders, such as myasthenia gravis or Parkinson’s disease. Aminoglycosides may exacerbate muscle weakness due to their potential curare-like effects on neuromuscular function. Bronchospasm Bronchospasm may occur with the inhalation of TOBI®. In clinical studies, changes in FEV1 (forced expiratory volume in one second) after inhalation were similar between the TOBI® and placebo groups. If bronchospasm occurs, it should be managed with appropriate medical treatment. Precautions Information for Patients A Patient Medication Guide is included in the TOBI® package, providing detailed instructions for proper use. Safety Information 1. Hearing Loss and Dizziness: TOBI® belongs to a class of antibiotics that have been associated with hearing loss, dizziness, kidney damage, and fetal harm. In clinical studies, ringing in the ears (tinnitus) and hoarseness were more commonly reported in patients taking TOBI® compared to those on placebo. 2. Cystic Fibrosis Symptoms: Patients with cystic fibrosis may experience various symptoms, some of which could be related to their medications. Any new or worsening symptoms should be reported to a healthcare provider. 3. Hearing Concerns: Patients should inform their doctor if they experience ringing in the ears, dizziness, or any changes in hearing. 4. Kidney Function: Patients with a history of kidney problems should notify their doctor before starting TOBI®. 5. Pregnancy: Women who are pregnant or planning to become pregnant while using TOBI® should discuss the potential risks with their doctor. 6. Nursing Mothers: Women who are breastfeeding should consult their doctor before using TOBI®.
